newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-SURPRISE AUXERRE WIN DEEPENS AJAX GLOOM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SURPRISE AUXERRE WIN DEEPENS AJAX GLOOM.

text.p: Unfancied Auxerre inflicted a shock 2-1 home defeat on four-times champions Ajax Amsterdam in a European Cup Champions' League match on Wednesday to leave group A wide open.
With Grasshopper Zurich losing to Glasgow Rangers, three clubs are level on nine points each.
While Auxerre entertain the Scottish champions, Ajax will have to dig deep to earn something from their December visit to Zurich.

Auxerre, needing to beat Ajax to keep alive their hopes of reaching the last eight at the first attempt, had a dream start when Bernard Diomede smashed home from short range after a clever back header from Lilian Laslandes.
Seconds later Diomede was centimetres away from adding a second but his snap effort shaved the post with Van der Sar stranded.

Midway through the first half, Ajax coach Louis van Gaal abandoned his starting formation, replacing right back John Veldman with 19-year-old debutant Arno Splinter, allowing skipper Ronald de Boer to push up into the middle.
Ajax clawed their way back into the game and drew level a minute before the break when Nigerian winger Tijani Babangida rounded Lionel Charbonnier in the Auxerre goal and scrambled the ball home.

Auxerre, playing confidently with three up front throughout, continued to press and Van der Sar was called into action to make saves from Marlet and Laslandes as the French side soaked up Ajax pressure and broke swiftly and dangerously on the counter.
Diomede crashed a left-foot shot against the bar just a moment before Babangida's equaliser and Auxerre could justly claim to have had much the better of the first half.

With injuries robbing Ajax of five regulars and Auxerre of six -- equivalent to an entire first team between them -- the game could have lacked fluency but, with Auxerre pressing for a winner and Ajax desperate to lift their increasingly dispirited supporters, it made for an entertaining spectacle beneath the Amsterdam Arena's closed glass roof.

With 11 minutes gone in the second half, Auxerre's Nigerian defender Taribo West powered through the home defence on a surging run and fed Marlet who sealed victory with a right-foot shot past Van der Sar.

There were few high points for the Dutch side, who continue to look totally out of sorts. Marc Overmars looked lively early on but his final ball let him down and Patrick Kluivert was at best a peripheral figure.

Coach Louis van Gaal admitted that qualification for the quarter-finals would now be difficult. "We're missing too much at the moment. We have most of the possession but we're creating too few chances," he said.

Portuguese striker Dani, who scored twice on his European debut against Rangers, blasted two efforts high and Kluivert failed to latch on to a loose ball in the Auxerre box in the final throes of the match.

Ajax Amsterdam: 1-Edwin van der Sar, 2-John Veldman (32-Arno Splinter 23), 5-Winston Bogarde, 29-Mario Melchiot, 30-Menno Willems, 6-Ronald de Boer, 19-Arnold Scholten, 16-Nordin Wooter (21-Dani), 7-Tijani Babangida, 11-Marc Overmars, 9-Patrick Kluivert

Auxerre - 1-Lionel Charbonnier, 12-Taribo West, 13-Frederic Danjou, 4-Franck Silvestre, 22-Eric Assati (31-Frederic Jay 70), 14-Christian Henna, 6-Philippe Violeau, 8-Moussa Saib, 17-Steve Marlet, 9-Lilian Laslandes (15-Abdelhafid Tasfaout), 11-Bernard Diomede (28-Patrice Lepaul 85)
